name: SwiftRoute Last-Mile Delivery Uniform Set
description:
SwiftRoute's last-mile delivery drivers cover every tier of GLMZ, from Shelf drop-offs to Spire concierge delivery, and their uniform reflects that range of environments. The set includes a weathershell jacket in SwiftRoute's cobalt blue with retroreflective silver trim on the shoulders, chest, and cuffs for visibility in low-light urban conditions; a moisture-wicking base-layer shirt; and reinforced cargo trousers with expandable knee panels for riders who spend shifts on electric cargo bikes. The jacket is waterproof to IP68 standard and rated for sustained operation in M88's frequently severe weather corridors along the lake. GPS routing hardware is woven into the left sleeve in a mesh antenna pattern that feeds directly to the driver's BCI delivery overlay.

The uniform is designed for constant motion: every closure is magnetic or snap-based for one-handed operation, and the collar seals quickly against weather without requiring both hands. Port-access panels are integrated at the left wrist for BCI scanning hardware used to authenticate deliveries. The jacket back panel is split-vent for geneware-modified riders with tail modifications, and the collar is sized generously for workers with neck or jaw augmentation. SwiftRoute drivers are tracked continuously via the GPS mesh; the uniform is, functionally, a monitoring device. Most drivers know this and have made their peace with it, or haven't.
cultural_context: SwiftRoute drivers are everywhere in M88 — they're one of the few worker categories that moves freely between tiers on a daily basis. The cobalt blue is recognized and mostly trusted; drivers have cultivated a reputation for reliability that's separate from any feelings about the corporation that employs them. The GPS tracking is an open secret that everyone pretends isn't there.
story_hooks: A driver's GPS mesh logs a route through a section of Tier 1 that SwiftRoute's official maps show as impassable rubble — but the route data shows regular traffic, suggesting an active community the corporation doesn't know about or is actively ignoring.
A package on a standard SwiftRoute manifest is flagged by the driver's BCI scanner as containing restricted biologicals — but the system immediately clears it and logs the flag as a false positive.

A driver who covers both Tier 1 and Tier 5 routes starts noticing that certain packages going up to the Spire are being returned, unopened, with no reason logged — and the return addresses don't exist.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, utilitarian delivery uniform that reads as organized motion—cobalt blue weathershell jacket with silver retroreflective striping that catches light at shoulders, chest, and cuffs. The silhouette is athletic and slightly tapered, built for speed and agility. Paired with dark reinforced cargo trousers featuring visible expandable knee panels. The overall impression is professional infrastructure: trusted, present, and constantly moving through the city.
physical_description.fit: Slim athletic through the torso with articulated sleeve construction; cargo trousers have a relaxed thigh with reinforced knee panel gussets that allow full range of motion for cycling or climbing. All closures designed for one-handed manipulation. Collar is generously sized to accommodate neck/jaw augmentation without constriction.
physical_description.primary_material: Weathershell jacket in treated synthetic composite (waterproof to IP68); moisture-wicking technical base-layer in recycled polyester blend; cargo trousers in ballistic-weave reinforced nylon with ripstop paneling at stress points.
physical_description.texture: Jacket exterior has a subtle matte finish with tactile retroreflective trim that feels slightly raised; interior is smooth technical lining with minimal drag. Trousers have a crisp weave with reinforced, slightly textured panels at knees and seat. Everything designed to shed water and resist snag.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary cobalt blue (SwiftRoute corporate identity) with silver retroreflective geometric striping on shoulders, chest, sleeve cuffs, and back panel. Dark charcoal or navy cargo trousers. Minimal branding—small SwiftRoute woven label only.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap chest panel; friction-fit magnetic wrist cuffs; snap-closure cargo pockets; split magnetic vents at jacket back. All closures operable with single hand or gloved hand.
distinctive_features: Mesh GPS antenna pattern woven into left sleeve—visible as subtle metallic threading
Split-vent jacket back panel accommodating tail-modified geneware
Port-access panel at left wrist with BCI scanning hardware integration points
Expandable knee panels on trousers for riders spending shifts on e-cargo bikes
Collar designed to seal quickly against weather without two-handed operation
Retroreflective striping positioned for visibility from vehicle-level and above
Reinforced stress-point paneling at seat, crotch, and inner thigh
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3: working professional. The uniform signals reliability and authorized access, worn by workers trusted enough to move between tiers daily. Not luxury (Tier 1) but distinctly above salvage tier.
physical_description.cultural_context: SwiftRoute drivers are infrastructure—they're everywhere in M88 and represent one of the few job categories with cross-tier mobility. The cobalt blue is recognized and carries a separate reputation from the corporation itself; drivers have cultivated trust as individuals. The GPS tracking hardware is an open secret; most drivers have made peace with the monitoring or simply accepted it as cost of employment. Wearing this uniform signals reliability, but also visibility and trackeability.
physical_description.condition_typical: Delivered in pristine condition but breaks in quickly to a 'lived-in professional' state—minor scuffs on knee panels, faint creasing where closures flex repeatedly, light weathering on sleeve edges. The retroreflective trim remains bright; the uniform is regularly replaced on rotation to maintain visibility standards and GPS hardware integrity.

Model posed mid-stride, captured from slightly above to emphasize the shoulder and chest striping. Urban warehouse backdrop with rain-slick concrete and distant neon signage.
